WHAT CHANGED IN main.tsx (192 lines, was 154; under the 250 target and the 400 cap):
- Removed the three static legacy imports (`resolveLiveSetupFromBuild`, `resolveShellMode`, `ShellModeRoot`). Those were the whole defect: they pulled `shell/frame.tsx` — the sole production site of `data-testid="cr.shell.root"` at :173 — into the bundle regardless of route.

Used in both places the step names: the conditional legacy import and the `gateDevelopmentQuery` call. The query gate and the mount gate are now the same fact, so no build can strip the selectors at runtime while still shipping the shell they select, or the reverse.
- `chooseRoot` keeps manager mode first, then takes the legacy branch only when BOTH `DevelopmentLegacyRoot !== null` (compile-time) and the gated query has exact `v1=1` (route request), wrapped in `<Suspense fallback={null}>`; otherwise `CordumApp`. Preserved unchanged: `mountControlRoom`'s exported signature and defaults, hash scrubbing, the single pairing attempt/retry closure, manager connection, StrictMode, ClockProvider, `CONTROL_ROOM_ROOT_ELEMENT_ID`, the `CONTROL_ROOM_ROOT_MISSING` throw, and `MOUNTED_CONTROL_ROOM_ROOT`.

ONE DESIGN DECISION THAT COST TWO ITERATIONS, DISCLOSED IN FULL because it is the non-obvious part of the diff. The plain form —
```tsx
const DevelopmentLegacyRoot = DEVELOPMENT_BUILD ? lazy(() => import("./development-legacy-root.js")) : null;
```
— typechecks, builds and fences correctly, but REDS TWO DEVELOPMENT CONTROLS I am forbidden to edit: `scaffold.test.tsx > mounts through the production entry point` and `> refuses closed at the real entry point when the build carries no credentials`. Diagnosed rather than assumed — I dumped the rendered DOM and got `<div id="root" />`, EMPTY. So the v1 branch was correctly taken (CordumApp markup would be present otherwise) and the Suspense fallback was still painted: `mountEntryPointAt` does `await act(async () => void (await import("./main.js")))`, which resolves the ENTRY module but not the lazy chunk the entry then requests, so the assertion reads the DOM one turn early.

Starting the request eagerly at module scope fixed one of the two. What fixes both is awaiting it — `DEVELOPMENT_BUILD ? await import("./development-legacy-root.js") : null` — so a development entry has the module in hand before `mountControlRoom` runs and Suspense resolves on the first attempt. The top-level await sits INSIDE the dead branch, so production emits neither the await nor the module; the 413 kB single-asset measurement above is the proof, taken after this change. `lazy` + `Suspense` are still the composition, as the step requires.
